subject: Proposal: Market Parity Framework for Geo-Level Compensation
messages:
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Market Parity Framework for Geo-Level Compensation

Hi team —

I'm attaching a short model (market_parity_model.xlsx) and a one-pager playbook (geo-index-playbook.pdf) that synthesize our recent calibration work for leveling and geo bands. The ask: I need a recommended offer approach for two immediate candidates in the StellarCloud pipeline (SC-4238) where the hiring manager is pushing for top-quartile in-country pay but Finance wants a more consistent global anchor.

Key points in the model:
- Base bands by level (E3–E5) using blended median of Redwood's benchmark + TalentBench panel.
- Geo multipliers calculated off a US-SF anchor with caps at +30% / -20% to limit outliers.
- An optional local premium bucket for hard-to-fill roles (security/systems infra).

Questions for this thread:
1) Do we accept the caps (+30/-20) or compress further for FY27 budgeting?
2) For StellarCloud offers, recommend exact bands and any one-off uplift language for counteroffers (e.g., relocation vs. local premium).
3) Any regulatory or procurement flags we need to surface before sending the LOIs?

I'm aiming to finalize language by EOD Thursday so talent can extend the offers Friday. Please review the attachments and put comments inline in the Drive doc (link below).

Thanks —
Sergio
Sr. Manager, Talent Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Market Parity Framework for Geo-Level Compensation

Thanks for this, Sergio — I read through both attachments. High-level thoughts:

- The multiplier approach is sound; I would prefer a slightly tighter cap of +25% on the upside for FY27 to control near-term offer velocity (we can test +30% as a pilot for 2 roles).
- For E4 (senior IC), the blended median you show aligns with our recent offer acceptance rates in EMEA, but please add a conversion to annual OTE for roles that commonly include variable comp.
- For StellarCloud specifically, Lina told us last week they have internal bands that are inflated vs. our US-SF anchor. If we want to be competitive, consider adding a one-time sign-on instead of permanently moving the base band.

Small nit: in tab 2 of the model, the sample candidate mapping uses ‘E4a’ which isn't in our canonical band taxonomy. Can you map those to the standard E3/E4/E5 labels?

I added comments on row 14 and the cap logic in the Drive doc. Also flagging procurement: any hire > $250k TCO needs pre-approval in the portal (Marcus, FYI).

- Laura
Director, People Operations
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Market Parity Framework for Geo-Level Compensation

Agree with Laura's conservative cap. A few operational points from Finance/Comp:

- Recommend we keep the permanent base movements to within +20% for FY27 unless the role is in the critical infrastructure hiring bucket. That reduces forecast variance.
- Approve sign-on as an experiment: classify as one-time expense and route through hiring approvals; sign-on must be explicitly in the offer template.
- For StellarCloud (related_account SC-4238): if a candidate is above our band by >15% we should require hiring manager justification and a short memo routed to Procurement for exception approval.

I've attached a small projected TCO table (pasted into the Drive sheet) with replacement and ramp assumptions that push us toward the tighter +20% cap, especially for the coming quarter.

Marcus
Head of Finance Operations (comp and budgeting)
From: Lina Gomez <lina@stellarcloud.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Market Parity Framework for Geo-Level Compensation

Hi Sergio —

Thanks for the transparency and the model. Quick Q from the hiring team here at StellarCloud: if Redwood applies a +20% global cap for Senior Infrastructure (E4), will we be able to include a localized allowance that is clearly time-bound (12 months) to help with retention in LATAM markets? We prefer a temporary allowance over inflated base.

If you can confirm the acceptability of a 12-month localized allowance (documented as a one-time recurring stipend subject to review), the hiring team feels comfortable moving forward with two verbal acceptances this week.

Best,
Lina Gomez
Head of Talent Acquisition
StellarCloud Inc.
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: lina@stellarcloud.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Market Parity Framework for Geo-Level Compensation

Lina —

We can accept a 12-month localized allowance for LATAM hires as a documented time-bound stipend, provided:

- The allowance is paid as a separate line item (not folded into base).
- We include a clause that it will be reviewed at 12 months and may be discontinued based on market movement/role performance.
- Any offer where the total cash (base + allowance) exceeds our band cap by more than 15% requires a short memo and Procurement sign-off before an LOI is issued.

Action items:
- Laura/Marcus: I'll update the model to reflect +20% permanent cap with a 12-month allowance option and circulate an updated playbook by Friday morning.
- Lina: if you can send the candidate names + target countries we'll map exact allowance projections and TCO.

Thanks —
Sergio
Sr. Manager, Talent Strategy
Redwood Inference
